Resolves #3782

Docs, embedded Docs in the Portal, and Toast now use the existing generated HighlightJS bundle and one shared pair of custom themes. Both committed classic packs and their duplicate supporting files are removed; the theme license is retained. Explicit classic-script overrides and app-relative custom themes remain supported.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, worker-mediated source views and repeated Toast edits) → L3 required. No runtime acceptance residual.

## AC Evidence

No structured ACs on #3782. The original intent is covered by removal of both duplicate packs, shared themes under `resources/lib`, and the development/distribution browser receipts below. Focused units cover loader ordering, custom paths, Docs theme choices, both external app generators and consumer-directory build output.

## Deltas from ticket

- Reuse the existing generated module instead of relocating another classic pack. The build writes to the invoking workspace. The shared loader resolves that root against the originating page in both workers and the main thread.
- Generators copy only shared themes and their license into the app's existing resource location, using the installed Engine's copy helper.
- Toast publishes one escaped code leaf and awaits its DOM update. This preserves repeat edits with the newer library, which replaces markup rather than retaining VDOM child ids. Docs also awaits the DOM update acknowledgement before highlighting received source. Repeated highlighting preserves existing line tables and completes the bundled line-number plugin synchronously. Empty source placeholders are left untouched until content arrives, avoiding the plugin's empty-line-array error.

Contract Ledger: `util.HighlightJs.load()` retains its zero-argument API and resolves `Neo.config.basePath` against worker `Neo.config.url.base` or main-thread `document.baseURI`. The consumer guard invokes the installed `build/all.mjs` from the workspace with installation/themes/threads/docs disabled, then verifies HighlightJS in the workspace and the other generated dependencies inside the Engine package. The main addon retains its remote methods, `highlightJsPath` classic override and theme-path behavior.

## Test Evidence

Local Chromium acceptance: **12/12 cases passed** across source, ESM, webpack development and webpack production. `test/playwright/e2e/portal/HighlightJsResources.spec.mjs` opens Docs/Portal source views through their UI, holds source delivery to exercise the empty placeholder, checks later line numbers and theme switching, repeats an unchanged-source highlight, and edits Toast twice with 6px code padding. The delayed-delivery control reproduced the hosted Portal error before the guard. A controlled DOM acknowledgement test separately failed before the source-publication repair and passes afterward. Dedicated workers and disabled service-worker caching keep fixture routing deterministic; Canvas-starting-point and offline-cache behavior are outside this test. Receipts are retained in `highlight-dom-ack-{source,docs,esm,development,production}`: the first source run had a browser-launch timeout before Docs started; its isolated rerun passed, and Portal/Toast passed in the first run.

A fresh `npm pack`/install consumer passed the complete `check-consumer-runtime-build.mjs` guard using the existing workspace build entrypoint, including the real dependency generation and Data/Canvas/App/Main compiles. The wrong-root negative control rejected both HighlightJS files when present only inside the installed package; the old guard accepted that layout. In the retained fresh fixture, an app generated by the installed `appMinimal.mjs` loaded both debug and minified bundles from workspace `dist/highlight`, highlighted JavaScript and rendered two numbered lines, without another highlighter build or copy. A 404 control at that workspace URL rejected as expected. The guard's dummy bootstrap was replaced with the ordinary MicroLoader, app map and theme map for this browser receipt; this is not a turnkey installer claim. The default addon and direct utility call ran on the main thread.

Earlier source/ESM consumer and actual App/Data/VDom-worker URL controls used a separate fixture with symlinked Engine/dependencies. The worker controls forced the old installed-package bundle URL to return 404 and verified that zero-argument `load()` requested the workspace bundle. That evidence remains separate from the fresh-install main-thread receipt.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted here (`Missing script`); local class-module-scope, examples-body-only, fixed-sleep and file-size guards ran. Hosted checks remain the PR's live authority.

## Post-Merge Validation

No merge-only acceptance step; human merge remains required.
